children.name: Reading excerpt
children.content:
Transactions can overlap in time. Isolation describes what one transaction can observe while another is changing data.

To reason about correctness, first identify the invariant you need to preserve. Then consider the possible order of reads and writes.

children.name: Assistant response
children.content:
Isolation controls what concurrent transactions can see.

Read committed sees committed changes at each statement.

Repeatable read keeps a consistent snapshot during a transaction.

Serializable provides the strongest isolation: concurrent work must behave like a serial order.

children.name: Full original learning goal
children.content: I want to become a Senior Backend Engineer and develop the skills required to design, build, scale, and maintain complex production systems independently, with a strong focus on Node.js, TypeScript, NestJS, and PostgreSQL. My goal is to move beyond framework-level knowledge and develop a deep understanding of software architecture, distributed systems, concurrency, database internals, performance optimization, reliability, security, and cloud infrastructure. I want to master system design, architectural trade-offs, design patterns, event-driven architecture, message queues, caching strategies, transactions, consistency models, observability, and production troubleshooting. I want to understand not only how technologies work, but why they work, when to use them, what their limitations are, and how to make sound engineering decisions. The learning process should identify gaps in my knowledge, challenge my assumptions, and prioritize practical problem-solving over memorization. I want progressively more difficult exercises, realistic production incidents, code reviews, debugging tasks, and system design challenges. My ultimate goal is to confidently lead the technical design of backend services, evaluate architectural alternatives, identify bottlenecks, and make well-reasoned engineering decisions at a Senior Engineer level, eventually progressing toward Software Architect or Tech Lead.

children.name: Full original learning goal
children.content: I want to become a Senior Backend Engineer and develop the skills required to design, build, scale, and maintain complex production systems independently, with a strong focus on Node.js, TypeScript, NestJS, and PostgreSQL. My goal is to move beyond framework-level knowledge and develop a deep understanding of software architecture, distributed systems, concurrency, database internals, performance optimization, reliability, security, and cloud infrastructure. I want to master system design, architectural trade-offs, design patterns, event-driven architecture, message queues, caching strategies, transactions, consistency models, observability, and production troubleshooting. I want to understand not only how technologies work, but why they work, when to use them, what their limitations are, and how to make sound engineering decisions. The learning process should identify gaps in my knowledge, challenge my assumptions, and prioritize practical problem-solving over memorization. I want progressively more difficult exercises, realistic production incidents, code reviews, debugging tasks, and system design challenges. My ultimate goal is to confidently lead the technical design of backend services, evaluate architectural alternatives, identify bottlenecks, and make well-reasoned engineering decisions at a Senior Engineer level, eventually progressing toward Software Architect or Tech Lead.
